title: Re-Volt/Cars
text:
This game has thirty one different kinds of cars that have an official name shown in Car Selection section, therefore their pictures will be provided for easier identification.

Cars will be described based on what they do, how fast they are, how much they accelerate, how heavy they are, how stable they are, and how controllable they are. Descriptions will start from the first to last car that appears in the game. Each statistic of any car can be buffed and/or nerfed by making backup directory of game's installation folder.

RC Bandit
thumb|Re-Volt as seen in carbox
thumb|RC Bandit
 Name: RC Bandit
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Rookie
 Speed: 32 mph (51 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.06 m/s²
 Weight: 1.2 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

RC Bandit is first car of Rookie rating and first car encountered in the game. RC Bandit is electric-powered buggy under the 4WD drivetrain that is undeniably well-balanced vehicle with favorable top speed of 32 mph (51 kph), providing fair level of challenge for it's competitors. RC Bandit has respectable acceleration, clocking in at 2.06 m/s². These traits make RC Bandit reasonably swift under many circumstances. RC Bandit's versatility is further improved thanks to it's marvelous off-road capabilities. As buggy, RC Bandit is very flexible under many forms of terrain and elevation, traversing through bumpy sections with ease while being stable all at the same time. RC Bandit handling characteristic sare it's turning radius and grip that are fairly loose yet controllable, allowing RC Bandit to pull off many fundamental techniques within the game, such as powersliding and reverse 180's, which RC Bandit can demonstrate reasonably thanks to this advantage. RC Bandit is fairly light, weighing at only 1.2 kilograms. Though not as dramatic due to it's speed, Pick Ups will still disrupt RC Bandit noticeably, especially with some of stronger Power-Ups like Clone Pick Up Power-Up. RC Bandit has high frequency to stay flipped necessitating use of manually flipping itself back up, due to it's body frame layout. Fortunately, these issues do not overshadow RC Bandit's accomplished capabilities. Overall, RC Bandit is all-around vehicle boasting many appreciable stats such as it's top speed, acceleration, handling, and off-road capabilities that allow you to easily adapt in many ways. Whether RC Bandit is used on open tracks such as Toys in the Hood 1 or bumpy and off-road environments such as Botanical Garden, RC Bandit is ultimately buggy suitable for any given scenario. RC Bandit is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time.

Dust Mite
thumb|Dust Mite as seen in carbox
thumb|Dust Mite
 Name: Dust Mite
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Rookie
 Speed: 31 mph (50 kph)
 Acceleration: 1,97 m/s²
 Weight: 1.2 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Dust Mite is second car of Rookie rating and second car encountered in the game. Dust Mite is electric-powered buggy under the 4WD drivetrain that has well-rounded top speed, reaching at 31 mph (50 kph), being on-par with faster cars of Rookie rating. Dust Mite is smallest buggy in the game, supplemented thanks to it's handling characteristics, which is Dust Mite's biggest advantage it brings into. Dust Mite has superb cornering ability and narrow turning radius because it's wheels turn very quickly according to the desired direction, allowing Dust Mite to change it's trajectory without many hassles. Dust Mite has excellent grip that assists in stability of turning, highlighting little risk of spinning out of control. All in all, Dust Mite's small size and handling traits generates great synergy, allowing it to demonstrates excellent performance in terms of response time, and enabling Dust Mite to dodge incoming havoc just by steering out of the way, as well as promoting Dust Mite's ability to navigate through narrow sections of many tracks. Despite its small and nimble looking stature, Dust Mite's acceleration is clocked in at unremarkable 1.97 m/s², making it fairly difficult for Dust Mite to reach it's top speed, but most importantly, having negative impact on it's handling benefits. As with most cars, slowing down is almost necessary before entering corner and Dust Mite is no exception. Main problem for Dust Mite is it's ability of exiting corners, which many players will find it sluggish during this process. Dust Mite's small buggy benefit also compromises it's weight of 1.2 kilograms because it will occasionally find trouble against contact with Pick Ups, accentuating strategy of dodging them instead of tackling it head on, which would be suitable for more heavier cars. Furthermore, Dust Mite has mediocre stability due to structure of its small wheelbase. Dust Mite will sometimes experience loss of control when landing hard from the drop-offs of Toy World 1, or when navigating consistent bumpy areas such as Stunt Arena. Similarly to RC Bandit, Dust Mite has high tendency to stay flipped, increasing usage of repositioning or manually flipping itself back. Overall, Dust Mite boasts fantastic handling in terms of both turning radius and grip, and when combined with its small size, makes itself outstanding in maneuverability. But, Dust Mite suffers from it's middling stability and acceleration stats. Fortunately, you can still use Dust Mite to effective nature, but you will need slightly higher level of skill than all-around vehicles in it's rating. Dust Mite is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time.

Phat Slug
thumb|Phat Slug as seen in carbox
thumb|Phat Slug
 Name: Phat Slug
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Rookie
 Speed: 31 mph (55 kph)
 Acceleration: 1.4 m/s²
 Weight: 2.5 kg
 Drivetrain: RWD

Phat Slug is third car of Rookie rating and third car encountered in the game. Phat Slug is electric-powered buggy under the RWD drivetrain that weighs in at massive 2.5 kilograms, making is heaviest in it's rating, and granting amazing resistance to Pickups with even strongest Power-Ups such as the Clone Pick Up Power-Ups or Bomb Power-Ups doing very little to it. Phat Slug mass is considered outlier, as most of it's competitors weigh around 1.4 kilograms or less. Phat Slug also possesses great cornering ability because it's front wheels are capable of locking to it's desired direction within less in second, bestowing Phat Slug with commendable turning radius that allows it to undertake corners without necessarily slowing down. Along with this, Phat Slug possesses satisfactory top speed, peaking at 31 mph (50 kph) much like Dust Mite. Phat Slug's stability is also decent, which is accredited to it's large shock absorbers and wheelbase. Sadly, Phat Slug has lots of flaws like it's grip with its adhesion on ground being occasionally unpredictable mainly due to it's RWD configuration. As such, Phat Slug demonstrates occasional problems with traction depending on the surface, not performing too well in the freezer section in SuperMarket 2 or the glass walkway in Museum 2. Phat Slug's most detrimental flaw is easily it's acceleration stat which is atrocious 1.4 m/s², making Phat Slug slowest accelerating car in its rating, and to broader extent, one of worst cars in the game. This is highly problematic because every competitor in the Rookie rating has acceleration stat that is at least acceptable or better, further isolating Phat Slug's performance from rest of it's rivals. Phat Slug's poor acceleration makes it very difficult to reach it's respectable top speed. Phat Slug suffers from exiting corners because it loses noticeable amount of speed when turning corners, forcing Phat Slug to rely on it's acceleration stat upon finishing corners. Additionally, Phat Slug has issues climbing various inclines such as escalator in Museum 2 where it loses significant amount of speed upon entering, while simultaneously navigating this section at slower pace than many of it's competitors, making Phat Slug very sluggish car under many circumstances. Overall, Phat Slug is vehicle of extremes that is heaviest car in Rookie rating thanks to it's immense mass of 2.5 kilograms and remarkable turning radius that provides assistance on corners. But, Phat Slug has one of worst acceleration stats in the game and awkward grip. Since almost all of it's competitors have terrific acceleration stats, Phat Slug horrific acceleration stat is considered outlier, which significantly outweighs its advantages, making Phat Slug very difficult car for you to win races with. Phat Slug is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time.

Col. Moss
thumb|Col Moss as seen in carbox
thumb|Col Moss as seen in carbox
 Name: Col. Moss
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Rookie
 Speed: 32 mph (52 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.14 m/s²
 Weight: 1.5 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Col. Moss (also known by it's full name Colonel Moss) is fourth car of Rookie rating and fourth car encountered in the game. Col. Moss is electric-powered car under the 4WD drivetrain that has remarkable top speed of 32 mph (52 kph), making Col. Moss fastest car in Rookie rating, and giving it advantage of navigating through straightaways at exceptional pace, allowing it to leave behind it's competitors. Col. Moss also has good acceleration of respectable 2.14 m/s², allowing Col. Moss to easily reach it's top speed, and making it intimidating in terms of swiftness. Col. Moss's has excellent grip that is extremely beneficial to car because it's very stable when cornering even at highest speeds. This is further supplemented from its 4WD drivetrain, allowing Col. Moss to drive under many surfaces such as freezer section in SuperMarket 2. Col. Moss's weight of 1.5 kilograms allows it to take direct hits from Pick Ups nicely. However, Col. Moss struggles with cornering because it has one of worst turning radius stats in it's rating because it has severe difficulties steering at various tight corners, not helped by it's high speed that necessitates use of braking or powersliding in order to complete corners. Col. Moss's disadvantage of having bad turning radius has large negative impact on Col. Moss's top speed due to it's inability to undertake corners at fast pace. Overall, Col. Moss has good top speed and exceptional traction. But, Col. Moss's dreadful turning radius and weakness in corners is significant impact on it's viability in races. So, if you want to use Col. Moss as your car, you must heavily on wide open tracks instead and utilize these sections in order to procure wins. Col. Moss is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time.

Harvester
thumb|Harvester as seen in carbox
thumb|Harvester as seen in carbox
 Name: Harvester
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Rookie
 Speed: 29 mph (47 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.28 m/s²
 Weight: 1.7 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Harvester is fifth car of Rookie rating and fifth car encountered in the game. Harvester is electric-powered car under the 4WD drivetrain that has spectacular handling characteristics, like it's very lenient traction that gris well under many different types of surfaces, which is further improved thanks to Harvester's 4WD drivetrain. Harvester's cornering ability is known to be among the best in its rating. Harvester's turning radius is also one of the tightest because it's wheels can lock quickly in specific direction, making Harvester capable of undertaking corners very easily. In fact, Harvester's turning radius is extremely outstanding that it enables it to drive through tightest corners under full throttle. Harvester also has great acceleration of 2.28 m/s² that is sufficient enough to prove handy under many circumstances, like recovering from mistakes. Synergy of Harvester's exceptional handling and credible acceleration stat makes it effortless in avoiding obstacles and havoc caused by Pick Ups. Harvester has remarkable weight of 1.7 kilograms that shows very little consequences if Harvester takes direct hit from Pick Ups instead of maneuvering away from it. Only problem for Harvester is it's very poor top speed of 29 mph (47 kph) that makes it slowest in it's rating and in game overall. Harvester's driving on straightaways is conspicuous because it will be very easy for vehicles such as Col. Moss or Dr. Grudge to catch up and overtake it, as well for many of competitors to leave behind Harvester in races if you are not careful while using it. Overall, Harvester is beginner-friendly car that requires very little skill to use because it possesses best handling characteristics in it's rating that allow it to turn and maneuver around through many corners and angles effortlessly. Harvester's acceleration and weight stats are also formidable, proving as valuable contributions in terms of recovery and resistance respectively. But, Harvester has horrendous top speed. As result, Harvester demonstrates great potential, proving very effective in tracks with many tight corners such as SuperMarket 1 or Toy World 2, but unsuitable in open tracks such as Toys in the Hood 1. Harvester is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time.

Dr. Grudge
thumb|Dr. Grudge as seen in carbox
thumb|Dr. Grudge
 Name: Dr. Grudge
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Rookie
 Speed: 31 mph (51 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.52 m/s²
 Weight: 1.4 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Dr. Grudge (also known by it's full name Doctor Grudge) is sixth car of Rookie rating and sixth car encountered in the game. Dr. Grudge is electric-powered car under the 4WD drivetrain that has either above average or well-balanced stats that are one of it's biggest and game-changing advantages. Dr. Grudge is has top speed of 31 mph (51 kph) that is very remarkable for it's rating, and good acceleration of 2.52 m/s² that ranks Dr. Grudge as second-fastest accelerating car in it's rating, allowing Dr. Grudge to recover quickly from obstacles or mistakes induced by players. Synergy of good top speed and acceleration give Dr. Grudge formidable agility that makes it very quick under many situations. Dr. Gurdge also has magnificent cornering abilities are magnificent as well because it's turning radius is very narrow thanks to it's wheels full-locking in desired direction relatively quicklym, allowing Dr. Grudge to steer at steep degree even at tightest corners, which further improves Dr. Grudge's swiftness that allows it to successfully undertake many corners at full speed. Only problem with Dr. Grudge is it's mediocre grip where it has high tendency to slide when it turns suddenly at high speed, evident from all four of it's wheels create skid marks when steering, indicating  possible chance of spinning out of control and oversteering if you drive carelessly on corners. Overall, Dr. Grudge has exceptional swiftness from combo of remarkable top speed and acceleration that allow it to perform well in many sections where it will frequently overtake it's competitors on both straightaways and corners. Although Dr. Grudge's grip is loose, necessitating the use of caution, it gives it amazing powersliding abilities which further supplements it's mobility. Ultimately, Dr. Grudge's advantages massively outweigh it's grip issues for which is considered one of best cars in it's rating thanks to it's exceptional stats across board, proving to be potent car for you to use. Dr. Grudge is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time.

Volken Turbo
thumb|Volken Turbo as seen ingame
thumb|Volken Turbo
 Name: Volken Turbo
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Rookie
 Speed: 30 mph (49 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.22 m/s²
 Weight: 1.6 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Volken Turbo is seventh car of Rookie rating and seventh car encountered in the game. Volken Turbo is electric-powered car under the FWD drivetrain that has decent weight of 1.6 kilograms that enables Volken Turbo to take impacts from Pick Ups with little trouble, fair acceleration of 2.22 m/s² which is positive aspect on mobility, with Volken Turbo demonstrating no major issues in terms of swiftness, preventing Volken Turbo from falling behind on it's competitors in terms of slanted hills and ramps. Volken Turbo has exceptional traction and best grip statistics due to being only FWD car in it's class that shows significant prowess on many surfaces compared to it's rivals, most notably freezer section in SuperMarket 2, where Volken Turbo is adhesive when turning in that section, making Volken Turbo as one of most stable cars in it's rating. Sadly, Volken Turbo has mediocre speed of 30 mph (49 kph) which is bad for straightaway sections of tracks, and wider turning radius where it will take longer for Volken Turbo's wheels to fully lock in desired direction, requiring modest amount of practice for you to conform it's handling characteristincs. Overall, Volken Turbo is all-around vehicle which is accredited from it's respectable acceleration, weight, and handling with emphasis on grip. But, Volken Turbo has middling top speed than rest of cars in it's class. Volken Turbo's FWD configuration may take time to get used to, but it will remain excellent choice for you to drive because it's suitable for almost any scenario. Volken Turbo is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time.

Sprinter XL
thumb|Sprinter XL as seen in carbox
thumb|Sprinter XL
 Name: Sprinter XL
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Rookie
 Speed: 31 mph (50 kph)
 Acceleration: 3.16 m/s²
 Weight: 900 g
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Sprinter XL is eighth car of Rookie rating and eighth car encountered in the game. Sprinter XL is electric-powered car under the 4WD drivetrain that has amazingly high acceleration of 3.16 m/s², making it useful in starting grids to pull ahead of opposing racers within seconds, avoiding minimal conflict in terms of packed collisions at start of race, quickly recover from making mistakes, and navigating inclines very quickly where it only uses minimal speed upon entering such sections. Sprinter XL has very respectable top speed of 31 31 mph (50 kph), which in combination with it's amazing acceleration grants it astounding swiftness. Sprinter XL also has narrow turning radius, giving it capability of undertaking corners at decent speeds. Sprinter XL is held back by it's abysmal 900 grams, making it highly suspectible to Pick Ups that can launch it significant distance away from impacts by Firework Power-Up, Firework Pack Power-Up, and Water Balloon Power-Up. Real problem of Sprinter XL is it's bad grip because it has below average tractions that exhibits problems under many surfaces like freezer section in SuperMarket 2 or any off-road terrain in general. Furthermore, performing very sharp turn at high speeds will more often cause Sprinter XL to lose control, which are issues most likely caused due to it's high acceleration. Because Sprinter XL accelerates quickly, this can cause lack of friction on ground, making it very vulnerable to spinning out of control if you are careless. Overall, Sprinter XL has good speed, extravagant acceleration, and turning radius. But, Sprinter XL has bad weight and it's tire grip on track that causes it to do spin-outs. Nevertheless, Sprinter XL's supreme acceleration is very praiseworthy and massive positive contribution to it's overall performance. However, if you want to fully capitalize Sprinter XL's advantages, you will need very high level of skill compared to other vehicles, requiring absolute track and racing skill from you. Sprinter XL is immediately unlockable upon starting the game for the first time.

RC San
thumb|RC San as seen in carbox
thumb|RC San
 Name: RC San
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Amateur
 Speed: 35 mph (53 kph)
 Acceleration: 3.15 m/s²
 Weight: 1 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

RC San is first car of Amateur rating and ninth car encountered in the game. RC San is electric-powered car under the 4WD drivetrain that has amazing acceleration of 3.15 m/s² which can rival acceleration of cars of it's class, and cars of higher classes, allowing it to pull out of starting grid very easily, recover from errors or obstructions with no issues, and climb inclines without losing noticeable amount of speed. RC San also has excellent turning radius that allows it to take very tight turns without needing to slow down, which is beneficial to it's cornering ability and overall performance. Coupled with it's high acceleration, tracks with many tight corners are best tracks for you to use RC San because it can traverse tight areas such as SuperMarket 1 much quicker than it's competitors. RC San also has also has acceptable top speed of 33 mph (53 kph). However, RC San weighs only one 1 kg, making it very vulnerable to Pick Ups like Firework Power-Up and Firework Pack Power-Up that will launch RC San significant distance away upon hit. RC San's traction is mediocre where it will occasionally find trouble with slippery areas such as backyard of Toys in the Hood 2. Overall, RC San is very potent, significant, and nimble car that boastssuperb acceleration, turning radius stats, and balanced top speed. But, RC San has low weight and substandard traction. Fortunaetly, RC San's flaws aren't problematic enough to overshadow it's strengths because RC San performs best at tracks with plenty of narrow and sudden corners. Using these sections while driving RC San will allow you to control race and procure wins. RC San is unlocked when you win Bronze Cup in Championship mode.

Candy Pebbles
thumb|Candy Pebbles as seen in carbox
thumb|Candy Pebbles
 Name: Candy Pebbles
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Amateur
 Speed: 34 mph (54 kph)
 Acceleration: 1.8 m/s²
 Weight: 1,3 kg
 Drivetrain: RWD

Candy Pebbles is second car of Amateur rating and tenth car encountered in the game. Candy Pebbles is electric-powered car under the RWD drivetrain that has decent top speed of 34 mph (54 kph), acceptable weight of 1.3 kilograms, which is satisfactory for its rating, being capable of taking hits from Pick Ups, but not too consistently. Candy Pebbles's best stat is it's cornering ability thanks to it's tight naroow radiues that allows it's front wheels to snap quickly to direction it turning. Candy Pebbles's turning radius is sufficient enough to provide it exceptional maneuverability in corners speed-wise, reducing necessity of using brakes upon entering corners. Sadly, Candy Pebbles's overall performance is also perplexed with some rather dull characteristics like sluggish acceleration of 1.8 m/s², and very dubious grip that makes it lag behind it's competitors at times. While problem with grip can be managed with extra caution and solid level of technical skill, Candy Pebbles has high tendency to slide, especially when speeding downhill at fast speeds, or abruptly making sharp turn. Overall, Candy Pebbles has decent top speed, weight, and excellent cornering ability. But, Candy Pebbles could use improvement in grip and acceleration that make it's performance middling at times. Nevertheless, Candy Pebbles can be good car if you can learn how to control it. Candy Pebbles is unlocked when you win Bronze Cup in Championship mode.

Genghis Kar
thumb|Genghis Kar as seen in carbox
thumb|Genghis Kar
 Name: Genghis Kar
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Amateur
 Speed: 35 mph (56 kph)
 Acceleration: 1.65 m/s²
 Weight: 2 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Genghis Kar is third car of Amateur rating and eleventh car encountered in the game. Genghis Kar is electric-powered car under the RWD drivetrain that has outstanding top speed of 35 mph (56 kph) that makes it great for driving straightaways at exceptional pace and overtaking many of it's competitors in wide open tracks like Toys in the Hood 1. Genghis Kar has impressive weight of 2 kilograms that allows it to take many impacts from Pick Ups with ease because it's quite resistant against strongest weapons, such as Clone Pick Up Power-Up. Genghis Kar's traction on road is very formidable because it has amazing grip regardless of it's speed, which further makes it more simple traversing in many tracks at high pace. Unfortunately, Genghis Khar suffers from underwhelming acceleration of 1,65 m/s² that is problematic in areas in slanted ramps, and unremarkable corneting ability that is plagued with Genghis Kar's slow steering rate, making it take a while for Genghis Kar's front wheels to fully lock in given direction, giving it wide turning radius, and losing significant amount of speed when it's wheels are turned all the way. But acceleration and cornering aren't real problem for Genghis Kar. Real problem with Genghis Kar is being unstable because it's prone to flipping over if you drive it continuously over bumps and corners, making use of Battery Power-Up very risky on Genghis Kar. Overall, Genghis Kar boasts amazing top speed and weight, but is immensely hindered from it's disappointing turning radius, and it's atrocious acceleration and stability, which are sadly prevalent enough to overpower Genghis Kar's advantages, causing it to demonstrate major difficulties in numerous tracks. So, if you want to use Genghis Kar, you will need very high skills in controlling because Genghis Kar is mainly good in wide open tracks. Genghis Kar is unlocked when you collect all Secret Stars in tracks of Easy difficulty in Practice mode.

Aquasonic
thumb|Aquasonic as seen in carbox
thumb|Aquasonic
 Name: Aquasonic
 Class: Glow
 Rating: Amateur
 Speed: 34 mph (54 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.37 m/s²
 Weight: 1,4 kg
 Drivetrain: RWD

Aquasonic is fourth car of Amateur rating and twelfth car encountered in the game. Aquasonic is glow-fueled car under the RWD drivetrain that has nice weight of 1,4 kilograms that allow it to tank impacts from certain Pick Ups easily. Aquasonic's decent top speed of 34 mph (54 kph) allows it to race nicely on straightaways and keep up alongside it's competitors without fear of falling behind. Aquasonic has comfortable acceleration of 2.37 m/s² that allows it to accelerate smoothly and recover from errors or obstructions. Aquasonic has exceptional turning radius that allows Aquasonic to take very tight turns without needing to slow down. Aquasonic also has modest traction that makes it controllable when turning and powersliding without fear of spinning out of control. However, Aquasonic has difficulties on very slippery surfaces like freezer section in SuperMarket 2, and sometimes in grassy areas in Toys in the Hood 2, due to little or no friction in those areas. Aquasonic's RWD drivetrain makes it vulnerable to Oil Slick Power-Up because it has tendency to oversteer at low speeds, caused by spinning rear tires during acceleration. Overall, Aquasonic is very multi-talented car that boasts well-rounded mobility, exceptional turning radius, and tolerable amount of grip under normal surfaces. But, Aquasonic is slightly vexed due to it's RWD configuration and dubious off-road capabilities. Nevertheless, Aquasonic's flaws at most are only nuisance, and aren't sufficient enough to overshadow it's glaring advantages. Ultimately, Aquasonic is excellent competitor in it's rating because it's well performing car suitable in many situations that doesn't involve slippery surfaces. Aquasonic is unlocked when you collect all Secret Stars in tracks of Easy difficulty in Practice mode.

Mouse
thumb|Mouse as seen in carbox
thumb|Mouse
 Name: Mouse
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Amateur
 Speed: 34 mph (54 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.86 m/s²
 Weight: 2,3 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Mouse is fifth car of Amateur rating and thirteenth car encountered in the game. Mouse is electric-powered car under the 4WD drivetrain that has incredible weight of 2,3 kg, allowing it to take impacts from Pick Ups without fear of being launched meters away upon impact. Mouse is also fast car with decent top speed of 34 mph (54 kph) and whopping acceleration of 2.86 m/s². Mouse also has fair turning radius and satisfying grip that make itless prone to spinning out. However, Mouse suffers from being very unstable because it has high frequency of staying flipped when it happens, increasing usage of requiring to flip itself back up, wasting precious time in most crucial moments. Mouse is very vulnerable to obstructions because it's wheels stick out of it's body frame. Mouse also has high tendency to flip when steering under effects of Battery Power-Up, making use of Battery Power-Up risky on Mouse. Overall, Mouse is decent car with good speed, high acceleration, and weight stats. But, Mouse has horrendous stability which while not as bad as that of Genghis Kar, it still requires you to keep close eye on if you want to use Mouse while turning and on bumpy terrain. But, unlike Genghis Kar, Mouse can demonstrate very high potential in return if you can control it's instabilities thanks to Mouse's remarkable swiftness and decent handling traits. Mouse is unlocked when you win all tracks of Easy difficulty in Single Race mode.

Evil Weasel
thumb|Evil Weasel as seen in carbox
thumb|Evil Weasel
 Name: Evil Weasel
 Class: Electric
 Rating: Advanced
 Speed: 36 mph (58 kph)
 Acceleration: 1.95 m/s²
 Weight: 1,5 kg
 Drivetrain: 4WD

Evil Weasel is first car of Advanced rating and fourteenth car encountered in the game. Evil Weasel is electric-powered buggy under the 4WD drivetrain that has pretty good top speed of 36 mph (58 kph). As buggy, Evil Weasel has good traction on the ground, meaning it's not too vulnerable to losing control if it drives over Oil Slick Power-Up. Evil Weasel's best advantage is being stable when cornering, allowing it to excel in wide open tracks like Toys in the Hood 1, and to easily pass slippery surfaces like in freezer part of Supermarket 2 with little problems. However, Evil Weasel has average acceleration of 1.95 m/s², small lag on acceleration that gives it difficulties of climbing on uneven terrain, wide turning radius that forces it to slow down slightly in corners in most circumstances, and dubious weight that makes it occasionally disoriented when struck by Pick Ups. Overall, Evil Weasel is good car for you to use in many scenarios because it has good top speed, grip, stability, and control that make it great in many tracks. But, Evil Weasel could be better car if it's acceleration, weight, and cornering ability could be improved. Evil Weasel is unlocked when you win Silver Cup in Championship mode.

Panga TC
thumb|Panga TC as seen in carbox
thumb|Panga TC
 Name: Panga TC
 Class: Glow
 Rating: Advanced
 Speed: 37 mph (59 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.11 m/s²
 Weight: 1,8 kg
 Drivetrain: RWD

Panga TC (also known in its Carbox as Panga Touring) is second car of Advanced rating and fifteenth car encountered in the game. Panga TC is glow-fueled car under RWD drivetrain that has nice top speed of 37 mph (59 kph), allowing it to travel straightaways at fast race and outrun it's competitors in those sections. Panga TC has decent and well-rounded acceleration of 2.11 m/s² that makes it more swift and mobile. Panga TC has weight of 1,8 kilgorams that allows it to take some impacts from Pick Ups with few issues. However, Panga TC's greatest weakness is it's stability because it has relatively stiff suspension, difficulties on bumpy terrain, cornering at high speed where it can flip over if you drive it continuously over bumps and corners that make use of Battery Power-Up fairly risky, and it's RWD drivetrain that gives Panga TC troubles in slippery areas like freezer section in SuperMarket 2. Overall, Panga TC is excellent in top speed and good at acceleration that allow it to dominate race using these advantages. But, Panga TC can be crippled by it's stability parameters at times, requiring firm level of technical skill from you to drive it effectively. Panga TC is unlocked when you win Silver Cup in Championship mode.

R6 Turbo
thumb|R6 Turbo as seen in carbox
thumb|R6 Turbo
 Name: R6 Turbo
 Class: Glow
 Rating: Advanced
 Speed: 36 mph (59 kph)
 Acceleration: 2.46 m/s²
 Weight: 800 g
 Drivetrain: FWD

R6 Turbo is third car of Advanced rating and sixteenth car encountered in the game. R6 Turbo is glow-fueled car under FWD drivetrain that has good speed of 35 mph (57 kph) and admirable acceleration of 2.46 m/s², giving it huge swiftness that allows it to excel on straightaways in open roads such as Toytanic 1 and Toytanic 2. R6 Turbo also has exceptional grip where it loses no control when turning, being very steady in corners, and decent turning radius that enables it to pass by corners at adequate speed, which is abnormal for FWD car. However, R6 Turbo's greatest weakness is it's atrocious weight of 800g that makes it lightest car in entire game, which in combination with R6 Turbo's tiny body frame make it extremely vulnerable to Pick Ups to the point that even weakest strikes from Firework Power-Up, Firework Power-Up, Water Balloon Power-Up, along with explosions from Clone Pick Up Power-Up and Bomb Power-Ups can launch R6 Turbo meters away upon impact that are so enormous to the point that controlling R6 Turbo will be very hard upon being hit, overpowering R6 Turbo's ability to recover effectively. Furthermore, R6 Turbo's weak weight and small stature heavily impacts it's stability because it has relatively stiff suspension that shows no mercy for R6 Turbo at all, making it likely to lose control upon landing impact like drop-offs in Toy World 1. R6 Turbo's small wheelbase makes climbing steep inclines dangerous despite having excellent acceleration, because it has tendency to roll over when driving on uneven off-road terrain.
